activities.title: A* vs BFS: same goal, different work
activities.objective: Compare frontier ordering, explored work, and shortest-path behavior for BFS and A* on the same maze.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response distinguishes search work from path quality, connects the heuristic to frontier ordering, and avoids claiming that A* is always faster.

activities.title: Why greedy search gets stuck
activities.objective: Explain local optima and compare greedy hill climbing with an escape mechanism such as simulated annealing or restart.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response states that no improving neighbor does not prove global optimality and explains how annealing or restart changes the search behavior.

activities.title: Safe, risky, or unknown?
activities.objective: Use percept evidence to distinguish a square that is proven safe, possibly hazardous, or unresolved.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response distinguishes unknown from dangerous, separates entailment from plausibility, and does not treat a probability estimate as proof of safety.

activities.title: What will DPLL do next?
activities.objective: Connect CNF structure to DPLL propagation, branching, conflict, and pruning.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response names the actual inference or branch evidence and explains that a branch conflict prunes that branch; global UNSAT requires exhausting the relevant alternatives.

activities.title: Base rates and false alarms
activities.objective: Connect prior prevalence, true positives, false positives, and posterior probability.

activities.title: Explaining away
activities.objective: Predict and explain how evidence for one cause can lower belief in another after conditioning on a common effect.

activities.title: Which neighbors get the vote?
activities.objective: Predict the selected neighbors and class, then connect k and distance to the vote.

activities.title: Fit the training set, fail the future
activities.objective: Separate training error from validation/test behavior as model capacity changes.

activities.title: Why nonlinearity changes capacity
activities.objective: Compare an affine-only network with a nonlinear representation and explain the decision-boundary change.

activities.title: Assign, move, repeat
activities.objective: Predict one assignment and centroid update, then explain the alternating k-means cycle.

activities.title: One convolution cell
activities.objective: Predict one output-cell multiply-and-sum before revealing the feature-map value.

activities.title: One Q-update
activities.objective: Predict an action, TD target, and update direction before stepping the learner.

activities.title: Same answer, less search
activities.objective: Explain why a safe alpha-beta cutoff can reduce evaluated work without changing the minimax result.

activities.title: Attend, then predict
activities.objective: Connect a controlled representation/attention change to the next-token probability distribution.

activities.title: A proposed call is not an executed action
activities.objective: Trace a proposed tool call through validation, authorization, execution, observation, and context update.
